---
title: "News: the Stata command"
description: >
  Versions of the Stata command powerape. The R package's changes are under
  News, R package.
---

The Stata command is a port of the R package and follows its releases; the
version it ports is named in `powerape version` and in every power
statement. The changes of the R package are listed in its
[news](../news/index.html).

## powerape for Stata 0.2.2 (2026-11-20)

* A difference-in-differences design whose two parallel-trends scales
  coincide is no longer called a mismatch. With `gap(0)` or `trend(0)` and
  no covariates that move the outcome, parallel trends mean the same on the
  index and on the probability scale, so either analysis is valid: `power`
  reports power, and `n`, `mde`, `powerat`, `alpha` and `statement` take the
  design. The design print says why.
* The note under the print of a mismatched design with covariates says
  that the probit or logit analysis centres near, not on, the covariate-free
  reading.
* `ppost()` on a panel gives a warning. `didpilot` with `id()` and
  `design(cross-sections)` no longer warns about a `rho()` that was not
  given. The help file says that rates drifting over a pilot's periods bias
  the estimated `rho()` downward.
* The command now follows version 1.12.2 of the R package. Results of the
  designs that were valid before are bit-identical to 0.2.1.

## powerape for Stata 0.2.1 (2026-11-20)

* `powerape dgp NAME, didpilot` with `covariates()` returned too high a
  `rho()`. In a difference-in-differences design `rho()` is the dependence
  between a unit's outcomes that is left given the covariates; covariates
  are constant over time and add dependence of their own. The pairs of
  outcomes in a pilot show the whole dependence, and 0.2.0 used that raw
  value together with the covariates, which counted part of the dependence
  twice and overstated power. With covariates the command now solves for
  the `rho()` at which the design has the pilot's share of pairs with the
  outcome in both periods; the raw correlation is kept in `r(pilot)` and
  printed. Designs built without covariates are unchanged.
* A warning for few units in one group. Robust and cluster-robust standard
  errors are too small when one group of a difference-in-differences design
  has few independent units, and more periods per unit do not help.
  `power`, `curve`, `n`, `mde` and `robust` now warn when fewer than 30
  units are expected in the smaller group (in repeated cross-sections:
  fewer than 30 observations in the smallest group-by-before/after cell;
  with a subgroup: in the smallest group-by-subgroup cell).
* The help file says that `rho()` is the correlation given the covariates
  and corrects the sentence about `signal()` and the linear panel analysis:
  a panel design with a larger `signal()` at the same `rho()` has more
  power, because its units are more alike over time.
* The command now follows version 1.12.1 of the R package. Results of the
  designs that existed before are bit-identical to 0.2.0.

## powerape for Stata 0.2.0 (2026-11-13)

* Difference-in-differences designs. `powerape dgp NAME, did` builds a
  design with a treated and a control group before and after one treatment
  date, as a panel or as repeated cross-sections, with one or several
  periods on each side and an optional binary subgroup. `powerape setatt`
  pins the effect on the treated in probability points, and
  `powerape trueatt` returns it.
* `trends()` sets the scale on which the untreated trends are parallel, and
  `analysis()` sets the analysis: probit or logit, or a linear probability
  model with robust standard errors. When the two differ, `power` and
  `curve` report a labelled rejection rate with the mean estimate, and the
  searches refuse the design.
* `power`, `curve`, `n`, `mde`, `robust` (also over `trends()`), `powerat`,
  `alpha` and `statement` take these designs under both engines.
  `powerape dgp NAME, didpilot` builds a design from pre-treatment data.
* The command now follows version 1.12.0 of the R package. Not ported from
  it: the three-way interaction design, and the linear probability analysis
  of the designs other than difference-in-differences.
* Results of the designs that existed before are bit-identical to 0.1.3.

## powerape for Stata 0.1.3 (2026-10-17)

* Panel designs calibrate about as fast as in the R package. A panel
  `powerape dgp`, `setape`, `setaie`, `trueape` or `trueaie` at the default
  `nint(1e5)` took about a minute and now takes one to three seconds, so
  robustness sweeps over panel scenarios and `mde` searches, which
  recalibrate at every step, take seconds instead of minutes. Every result
  is bit-identical to 0.1.2.
* The validation scripts run from a clone of the repository and are part of
  it; see [How powerape is validated](validation.html).

## powerape for Stata 0.1.2 (2026-10-16)

* Every simulation command (`power`, `curve`, `n`, `mde`, `robust`) prints a
  line beginning `fit:` that names who fitted the simulated studies, for
  example `probit via engine(stata), effects(closed)`,
  `cfprobit via engine(stata), effects(margins)` or
  `Mata engine (Fisher scoring)`, and stores it in `r(fit)`, `r(engine)` and
  `r(effects)`.
* `engine()` and `effects()` given on a single command now apply to that
  command only. Before, they also changed the session default that
  `powerape engine` sets.

## powerape for Stata 0.1.1 (2026-10-16)

* Installation with `net install` (`powerape.pkg`, `stata.toc`), and
  `powerape version`, which checks that the command and its Mata library
  belong together.
* Declared for Stata 16 or later (frames). The control-function route under
  the default engine uses `cfprobit` (Stata 18 or later).
* `separation(keep)` under `engine(stata)`: replications with an empty
  identifying cell are fitted with `asis` and kept, as R's `glm` keeps them.
* `effects(margins)` for the interaction effect on the control-function
  route: `margins, dydx() at()` after `cfprobit`, with the control function
  held fixed.

## powerape for Stata 0.1.0 (2026-10-15)

* First release: a port of the R package powerape 1.11.3 with every route
  (parametric, pilot data, fitted pilot model, panel, control function),
  estimand (APE and AIE), claim and search of the R package. Validated
  against the R package in four tiers; see
  [How powerape is validated](validation.html).
